children: Accelevation Holdings Corp., a maker of power distribution and white-space infrastructure for data centers, filed for an initial public offering. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker “ACCV.” Proceeds will primarily be used to acquire units of its operating subsidiary and repay a portion of outstanding debt.

Accelevation designs, manufactures, and installs power distribution and white‑space infrastructure for mission‑critical data centers. Its integrated platform combines engineering, domestic manufacturing and nationwide field installation to deliver modular systems, thermal containment, structural solutions, and compact high‑density power products. The company’s portfolio centers on two categories: Infrastructure Solutions (including the SkyBridge modular platform, TechFrame steel structures and conveyance, thermal products, and installation/lifecycle services) and Power Products (branch circuit whips, remote power panels including 1,200‑amp high‑density RPPs, PDUs and related monitoring/upstream offerings). By unifying design, factory assembly and field execution under one provider, Accelevation aims to reduce deployment complexity, accelerate schedules and enhance accountability for hyperscale, colocation, AI and cloud customers.

Accelevation operates an expanding U.S. manufacturing footprint and leverages an engineering team with cross‑disciplinary expertise in mechanical, electrical, structural and thermal design. This vertical integration supports faster lead times, customization at scale, and the shift of white‑space work from the field into controlled factory environments. The company reports deepening relationships with large data center developers and hyperscalers, growing power product content per deployment, and increasing adoption of modular delivery as AI workloads drive higher rack densities and greater coordination across power, cooling and structural systems.
: Actionable data center TAM of $22.0 billion in 2025, projected to reach ~$80 billion by 2030.
: Expected ~30% CAGR for the company’s actionable TAM; new U.S. IT load projected to grow from ~6.5 GW (2025) to ~14.8 GW (2030) at an 18% CAGR.
: Vertically integrated “Design. Manufacture. Install.” platform; engaged with three hyperscalers at full-platform design level; $1.1 billion backlog as of June 30, 2026.
: Vertiv, Schneider Electric, Eaton, Tate; broader peers include nVent, GE Vernova, Forgent Power.

: Rising AI-driven rack densities, growing adoption of modular and prefabricated white-space solutions (penetration ~70% today to ~85% by 2030), and accelerating demand for advanced power products (power products TAM from ~$10.4B in 2025 to ~$35.5B by 2030).
: Hyperscale, colocation, AI and cloud data center operators; engaged with three hyperscalers at total platform design level.
: ~1.1 million sq. ft. of manufacturing capacity across southwest Ohio (~625k sq. ft.), Memphis, TN (~225k), Houston, MS (~220k) and Richmond, VA (~57k).
: U.S.-based manufacturing with nationwide field services and installation crews.
: Preferred supplier and master supply relationships embedded in certain customer standards; coordinated delivery with general contractors and end users.
: Backlog of approximately $1.1 billion as of June 30, 2026; book‑to‑bill of ~2.5x for the six months ended June 30, 2026.

: Modular bookings of ~ $700 million since initial development in September 2025; >50 engineers delivering ~700 custom designs annually; 1,716 employees as of June 2026 (including ~800 field services and ~745 manufacturing); branch circuit whips generated ~$71 million of revenue in 2025; average revenue per customer increased from ~$0.7 million in 2023 to ~$3.9 million in 2025.
, Chief Executive Officer - Co‑founded Accelevation in 2017; prior roles at Senneca Holdings, Valspar, Ecolab and General Mills; entrepreneur with multiple startups and patents.
, Chief Financial Officer - Former EVP & CFO at Rollins and CFO/CSO at MSA Safety; earlier career at KPMG; >25 years in finance, strategy and capital markets.
, Chief Transformation Officer - Former CFO of Accelevation; prior finance and transformation leadership at Corsearch, Senneca Holdings and others.
, Chief Operating Officer - Former President roles at Apogee Enterprises; earlier leadership at Valspar and NewPage; >25 years in manufacturing and supply chain.
, SVP, Operations - Joined from Amazon operations leadership; previously at GE Aviation; >16 years in supply chain leadership.
: Morgan Stanley; J.P. Morgan; Goldman Sachs; Barclays; BofA Securities; Houlihan Lokey; Baird; William Blair; Piper Sandler; Wolfe | Nomura Alliance
: Acquire Series A units of its operating LLC, then repay a portion of borrowings under its Credit Agreement, pay offering/transaction expenses, and for general corporate purposes.
